Indian Standard 

METHODS OF TEST FOR CABLES 
PART 61 FLAME RETARDANT TEST 



1. Scope — Covers a method to assess the ability of electric cable to resist ignition and to prevent 
fire from spreading. 

o 2. Significance — The way a cable behaves in a fire depends on the material and the design of the 

^ cable as well as the external circumstances. A cable is considered flame retardant if it, when being 

c^ tested, is ignited but extinguishes again when the external heat supply ceases and the spread of the 

^ fire does not exceed the given maximum value. 

in 

Q 3. Terminology — See IS : 1885 (Part 32)-1971 'Electrotechnical vocabulary: Parf 32 Cables, 
w conductors and accessories for electricity supply'. 

o 4. Apparatus — The test equipment shall consist of a vertical steel tube having a wall thickness of 

0.8 ± 0.1 mm with rectangular ventilation openings, a lid of steel and an edged conical tray of stainless 
^ steel for a volume of 1 litre of ignition fluid. The mass of the tray shall be 160 ±20 g. The complete 
^ equipment with all dimensions is shown in Fig. 1. The tray shall be placed on a heat insulating 
^ bedding. 

^ It shall be possible to vary the distance between the lid and the tube between 10 and 30 mm. 

in 

u At the upper end of the tube, there shall be a horizontal steel rod for suspension of the test 

H specimen described in 6. At the lower end of the tube which shall be open, the test specimen is fixed 
^^ with a metal wire with a maximum diameter of 0.8 mm. 

^ When adjusting the lid according to 8.1, the temperature in the tube is measured about 130 mm 

u from its upper end. 

<^ 5. Material 

5.1 Ignition Fluid — Ethanol 95 percent with a specific heat energy of about 23 MJ/kg. 

6. Test Specimen 

S 6.1 Test specimen shall consist of one cable or several cables cabled together with a lay of between 
^ 10 and 15 times as cabling diameter. The cabling diameter is the circumscribed circle of the test 
t^ specimen. The length of the test specimen shall be 850 mm in a finished condition. 

c 

^^ 6.2 Number of Specimens — When testirg single-core cable with an external diameter less than 4 mm, 

^ five pieces of the cable are cabled to one test specimen. When testing single core cable with an 

u external diameter equal to or larger than 4 mm but less than 10 mm, three pieces of the cable are 

H cabled to one test specimen. When testing a single core cable with an external diameter equal to or 

^^ larger than 10 mm and when testing multiconductor cables, one piece of cable is used as test 

^ specimen. 

B The external diameter of the test specimen shall not exceed 70 mm. 

B 
o 

^ 7. Conditioning — No pre-conditioning of the test specimen is required. 

a 

S 8. Procedure 

in 

g 8.1 Calibration of the Test Equipment — Before the test the test equipment shall be calibrated as 
3 follows: 

^ 20 X f ml (not less than 70 mm) ethanol 95 percent with a specific heat energy of about 

% t = K^-- mm '^^ '"^ ^^^ ^^^' ^''^V' where f is the burning time of ethanol in minutes, 

and K = 1 for a cable with a cross-sectional conductor area <2.5 mm^, 

K = 2 for a cable with a cross-sectional conductor area >2.5 mm^, and 
D = external diameter of the test specimen in mm.

FIG. 1 TEST EQUIPMENT FOR FLAME RETARDANT TEST 

The distance between the Hd and the tube is determined so that the temperature 255±5°C is 
obtained, at the point measured about 130 mm from its upper end, after that the ignition fluid has been 
burning for 3 minutes. This is done by burning a cerain quantity of ignition fluid (20 x t) as above 
and reading the temperature after 3 minutes. If necessary, the procedure is repeated after the test 
equipment has cooled down and with the lid in another position until the correct temperature has 
been reached. 



8.2 Placing of the Test Specimen — After the test equipment has cooled down the test specimen is 
placed in the tube with its longitudinal axis along the centre line of the tube. The test specimen shall 
be provided with a loop at one end and be suspended on the steel rod which is placed over the upper 
end of the tube so that the lower part of the test specimen extends about 50 mm below the lower 
part of the tube. The lower part of the test specimen is horizontally fixed with a metal wire with a 
maximum diameter of 0.8 mm. When testing, a quantity of ethanol (20 x t ml) is ignited and shall 
burn for t minutes. The fire is extinguished by taking out the fuel tray.

IS : 10810 (Part 61) - 1988 

8.3 The fire in the test specimen shall extinguish by itself. The testing is not finished until all signs 
of burning, including smoke without visible flame, have ceased.
